text: Then King Darius issued an order, and a search was made in the archives where the treasures were stored in Babylon.
And at Ecbatana, in the fortress in the province of Media, a scroll was found, and this is what was written in it:

"In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued this order concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: Let the house be rebuilt as a place for offering sacrifices, and let its foundations be laid. Its height shall be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits,
with three courses of dressed stone and one course of timber. The cost is to be paid from the royal treasury.

Moreover, the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, are to be returned. They shall be brought back to their place in the temple in Jerusalem and deposited in the house of God."
Now then, Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates, the officials of Beyond the River: keep far away from there.

versions.text: Now then, Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and you their associates, the officials of Beyond the River: stay away from there.
versions.explanation: The phrase "and you their associates" mixes second and third person awkwardly; the Aramaic has simply "and their associates." Removing "you" reads more smoothly aloud and matches the source. "Keep far away" also renders רַחִיקִין הֲווֹ a little more forcefully.

text: Leave the work on this house of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its site.

I also issue this decree concerning what you are to do for these elders of the Jews in the building of this house of God: the cost is to be paid in full to these men from the royal treasury, out of the tribute of Beyond the River, so that the work is not halted.

Whatever is needed—young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, along with wheat, salt, wine, and oil—is to be given to them daily without fail, according to the word of the priests in Jerusalem,
so that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
I further decree that if anyone alters this order, a beam shall be pulled from his house, and he shall be impaled on it, and his house shall be made a ruin because of this.

And may the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to alter this or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued this decree; let it be carried out with all diligence.
Then Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates carried out with all diligence exactly what King Darius had sent word to do.

So the elders of the Jews went on building and prospering through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished the building according to the command of the God of Israel and the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.

versions.text: So the elders of the Jews went on building and prospering, encouraged by the preaching of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished the building according to the command of the God of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia.
versions.explanation: The Aramaic reads מֶלֶךְ פָּרָס, singular "king of Persia," attached to Artaxerxes; the plural "kings of Persia" adds an interpretation not in the text. Also בִּנְבוּאַת is "prophesying/prophecy" rather than the more generic "preaching."

versions.text: So the elders of the Jews went on building and prospering through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished the building according to the command of the God of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
versions.explanation: The Aramaic וּמִטְּעֵם is singular, matching the singular מִן־טַעַם earlier in the verse; a single decree is envisioned as renewed by successive kings. The singular also keeps the parallel with "the command of the God of Israel" and reads more evenly aloud.

text: This house was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
Then the people of Israel—the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the returned exiles—celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy.

For the dedication of this house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel twelve male goats, one for each of the tribes of Israel.
They installed the priests in their groups and the Levites in their divisions for the service of God in Jerusalem, as prescribed in the book of Moses.
On the fourteenth day of the first month the returned exiles kept the Passover.

For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together; all of them were clean. They slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the returned exiles, for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.

versions.text: The priests and the Levites had purified themselves; all of them were clean. They slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the returned exiles, for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
versions.explanation: The word כְּאֶחָד ("as one," "together") is not represented, and the connective כִּי linking this verse to the previous one is dropped, weakening the flow of the narrative when read aloud.

text: So the Israelites who had returned from exile ate it, together with all who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.

For seven days they kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread with joy, because the LORD had filled them with joy and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, so that he supported them in the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.
